description: An address-identifier OPERAND (ISO §2023:8.4.3.1.2 identifier Format 9: the §2023:8.4.3.11 data-address-identifier ADDRESS OF identifier-1 or the §2023:8.4.3.13 program-address-identifier ADDRESS OF PROGRAM ...) outside the SET formats that gate themselves - the CALL argument §2023:14.9.4.3 SR3/SR4 name (kb/Work PB239: bare, BY REFERENCE, BY CONTENT or (Format 2) BY VALUE, always a sending operand that crosses as a detached pointer value), the INVOKE argument §2023:14.9.23.3 SR9/SR19 name (bare, BY REFERENCE, BY CONTENT, and the §2023:8.4.3.4 inline form's argument) and the §2023:8.8.4.2.2 Format 3 relation operand (kb/Work PB1021). A COBOL-2002 introduction, with the pointer classes. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 identifier is a function-identifier or a data-name with its qualifiers, subscripts and reference modifier, §1985:IV.4.3.8.5.1: "identifier is a term used to reflect that a data-name, if not unique in a program, must be followed by a syntactically correct combination of qualifiers, subscripts, or reference modifiers", and a CALL operand is a data item, §1985:X.5.2.3 SR3: "Each of the operands in the USING phrase must have been defined as a data item in the File Section, Working-Storage Section, Communication Section, or Linkage Section"; ADDRESS is no 1985 reserved word, since §2002:F.1 item 6 ("The following reserved words have been added") lists it. §2002:8.4.2.11 adds the identifier, "A data-address-identifier references the unique data item that contains the address of a data item" (§2002:8.4.2.11.3 GR1: "Data-address-identifier creates a unique data item of class pointer and category data-pointer that contains the address of identifier-1"; §2002:8.4.2.12: "A program-address-identifier references the unique data item that contains the address of a program"), and admits it as a CALL argument, §2002:14.8.4.2 SR3: "Identifier-2 shall reference an address-identifier or a data item defined in the file, working-storage, local-storage, linkage, or communication section"; §2002:F.2 item 103 states the class: "A new class of data is introduced, a pointer type which holds data and program addresses in a machine-specific or system-specific way." §2014:8.4.2.11 and §2014:14.9.4.2 SR3 carry the 2002 text (2014 drops only the communication section), as do §2023:8.4.3.11.1, §2023:8.4.3.13.1 and §2023:14.9.4.3 SR3. Recognition gate on the addressIdentifier rule, so every future surface that spells the identifier through it is gated automatically.
